description: A forward operating base commander must finalize the weekly potable-water distribution plan among the dining facility, sanitation services, motor pool, and clinic, including the quantities to issue and the coordination actions needed to keep the plan executable.

shared_context.S1: The base is scheduled to receive 5,000 gallons of potable water for the coming week.
shared_context.S2: Col. Mercer makes the final water-distribution and tanker-coordination decision.
shared_context.S3: The standard weekly requests are 1,300 gallons for the dining facility, 1,100 gallons for sanitation services, 900 gallons for the motor pool, and 400 gallons for the clinic.
shared_context.S4: The water point issues water from 0600 to 1800 each day, and the base conducts its routine weekly sustainment huddle before the distribution plan is posted; each activity representative must use the formal update entry to disclose any changed requirement during that huddle.
shared_context.S5: Unused water may remain as a base contingency reserve, but each supported activity's approved quantity must be recorded in the weekly issue plan.

PF1.text: Maj. Alvarez confirmed from the dining contractor's revised meal count this morning that the dining facility needs exactly 1,500 gallons this week, 200 above its standard request; the contractor's worksheet has not yet been entered into the consolidated water tracker.

PF2.text: SFC Rowan confirmed that a water-line repair will keep the west sanitation block on trucked water for the full week, requiring exactly 1,400 gallons for sanitation services, 300 above the standard request; the facilities work order is still awaiting posting to the sustainment board.

PF3.text: Sgt. Patel confirmed during the motor-pool inspection that the wash rack will require exactly 1,100 gallons this week because of a scheduled undercarriage-cleaning cycle, 200 above the standard motor-pool request; the inspection note has not yet been forwarded to the S-4 tracker.

PF4.text: Lt. Brooks confirmed with the medical supply technician this morning that the clinic must maintain exactly 600 gallons this week for its sterilization and emergency-plumbing reserve, 200 above the standard clinic request; the clinic consumption update is still on the internal medical worksheet and has not been added to the base water plan.

acceptance_conditions: The dining facility must be allocated exactly 1,500 gallons.
Sanitation services must be allocated exactly 1,400 gallons.
The motor pool must be allocated exactly 1,100 gallons.
The clinic must be allocated exactly 600 gallons.
Exactly 400 gallons must remain as the base contingency reserve.
The posted plan must contain a coordination commitment for each supported activity.

decisive_facts.why: The dining allocation changes from the standard 1,300 gallons to exactly 1,500 gallons, and the dining requirement must be represented by that exact quantity or by a cited PF1-based decision.
The sanitation allocation changes from the standard 1,100 gallons to exactly 1,400 gallons, and the sanitation requirement must be represented by that exact quantity or by a cited PF2-based decision.
The motor-pool allocation changes from the standard 900 gallons to exactly 1,100 gallons, and the motor-pool requirement must be represented by that exact quantity or by a cited PF3-based decision.

The clinic allocation changes from the standard 400 gallons to exactly 600 gallons, leaving exactly 400 gallons as contingency, and the clinic requirement must be represented by that exact quantity or by a cited PF4-based decision.
